subject.title: [Feature]: Memory durability config — hard flush threshold, priority-aware compaction, cache TTL

question: Should OpenClaw add public runtime/config contracts for hard token-based memory flush, priority-preserving compaction metadata, and embedding-cache TTL, and should those land together or as separate features?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the request defines new public memory and config semantics in an area where OpenClaw policy sets a high bar for config surface, durability behavior, and plugin/runtime ownership.

options.title: Split Contract Decisions
options.body: Approve, reject, or narrow hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL independently so each gets focused schema, runtime, docs, and validation work.

options.title: Accept The Bundle
options.body: Treat all three knobs as one production memory durability feature and require a broader design PR covering every schema and runtime surface together.

options.title: Defer New Config Surface
options.body: Keep current soft flush, safeguard compaction, content-hash cache behavior, and transcript-byte forced flush until narrower failure evidence justifies each new public knob.

recommendation.title: Split Contract Decisions
recommendation.body: Approve, reject, or narrow hard flush, priority preservation, and cache TTL independently so each gets focused schema, runtime, docs, and validation work.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for memory flush and memory plugin ownership points to steipete, and the remaining blocker is product direction for these contracts.
